correctness.rationale: For the exact bordered F19 sign convention, the independent integer replay verified skew-symmetry and all 400 conference-identity entries, and classified all 38,760 unordered six-subsets by four- and six-Pfaffian squares. The six counts in the stated order were 1140, 6840, 13680, 6840, 7980, 2280. The same 1140 masks in the first bin became transitive after switching a designated vertex to a source (remaining outdegrees 0,1,2,3,4). This test is invariant for the switching-transitive class: starting from a transitive order, switching an interior vertex to a source just rotates the two blocks of the other vertices. The largest t for the first cubic is 7+4 sqrt(3); the competing maxima are 6+sqrt(33), a root in (10,11) beyond which its cubic is increasing, 5+2 sqrt(5), 7 and 9. The Parseval normalization and equality of nonzero Gram and erased-vector operator spectra give the claimed sharp positive surviving bound and sharp error. The replay is /workspace/branches/3a261c25-3a71-4d81-8d52-bdf2b142412e/replay_six.py (full_run.txt in the same directory); the supplied trace/Bareiss, matching-Pfaffian and universal-sign scripts were inspected, not executed. No conclusion about optimality among frames is needed.

value.rationale: The explicit Paley conference frame is a standard structured benchmark; principal Gram spectra determine robustness under a natural family of erasures. A complete distribution over equally likely six-erasures gives the full discrete loss distribution, the exact frequency of worst cases, and a structural test for them, information not delivered by a worst-case bound or an arbitrary-six-matrix possibility list. This is a useful exact classification of the fixed frame rather than a new universal frame theorem.
